newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard to buy Verifone for $1.18 billion.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard to buy Verifone for $1.18 billion.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Wednesday it agreed to acquire VeriFone Inc. in a stock swap worth $1.18 billion in a bid to extend the company's position as a leader in electronic commerce.

Hewlett-Packard said VeriFone, which is a leader in electronic payment hardware and software, will be operated as an independent unit of HP. Verifone stockholders will receive one HP share for each VeriFone share, the company said.

The acquisition of VeriFone is a big step in HP's drive to develop businesses for what it calls the "on-ramps" and "off-ramps" of the information superhighway, a business that includes computer printers and scanners, where Hewlett-Packard already has a dominant market share.

In an intervew last week, the company's top Internet executive, Ira Goldstein, said Hewlett-Packard aims to become the information appliance supplier to the fast-growing market for Internet technology.
The Internet portion of the electronic commerce market alone is expected to reach $95 billion in the United States by the year 2000, according to research by International Data Corp.

Hewlett-Packard said the proposed acquisition would combine its strength as the second-largest U.S.-based computer equipment company with VeriFone's leadership in electronic commerce. VeriFone had net revenue of $472 million in its 1996 fiscal year.
